newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trades steady around 3.05 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money trades steady around 3.05 pct.

text.p: German call money began the new week largely unchanged trading around 3.05/3.075 percent with dealers saying rates were unlikely to come off further in the next few sessions.

Dealers said trading was mostly in equilibrium and that despite some market speculation about a possible rate cut by the Bundesbank, money market dealers largely shrugged off such talk saying a rate cut would be rather unlikely this week.
Many dealers instead predicted the central bank, seen to be under no pressure to act on rates as the dollar has appreciated considerably recently, would keep the money market rate steady.
The policy-making central bank council will meet on Thursday. Germany's main money market rate, the repo rate, has been kept unchanged at three percent since late August.
Banks held 39.7 billion marks in non-interest bearing accounts at the Bundesbank on Friday with the banks' monthly reserve average standing at 40 billion marks on Sunday.
